messages:
Alex K: Hey team — just pulled Feb invoices and there's a ~$23k line labeled 'Network Egress - EIP reassignment' for us-central1. Not sure what triggered it. Anyone seen this?
Maria S: I noticed a weird spike too, thought it was GPU churn during the rollout last Wed.
Jess (FinOps): Can you paste the invoice line or billingIDs? I'll correlate with the consolidated invoice.
Alex K: Here are the two suspicious rows from the billing export:
```
line_item_id,description,product,region,amount_usd
LI-987654,Network Egress - EIP reassignment,Network,us-central1,11640.00
LI-987655,Network Egress - EIP reassignment,Network,us-central1,11600.00
```
Samir Patel: billing-bot flagged a cost anomaly the morning after the scale event. Ran /bill-lookup LI-987654 and it points to multiple VMs detaching/reattaching external IPs during autoscale in the GPU pool.
billing-bot: :rotating_light: Cost anomaly detected for project redwood-prod: LI-987654, LI-987655. Suggested action: open ticket with cloud provider.
Maria S: That matches — during the horizontal downscale we moved GPUs between zones and the autoscaler replaced instances, which reattached ephemeral external IPs. I didn't expect egress charges for EIP reassignments though.
Samir Patel: Quick check of net logs shows large inter-zone data transfers while instances drained: 1.2TB transferred between us-central1-b and us-central1-c within 30m. Cloud vendor bills cross-zone egress for reassigned public IP traffic.
Jess (FinOps): Oof. Is this double-billed anywhere (compute + network)? Or strictly network line items?
Alex K: Appears as network-only but the amounts are split into two large lines — maybe two separate billing accounts (prod vs infra). Could be duplicate billing run.
Samir Patel: I ran a reconciliation: the UUIDs in the two lines have distinct account IDs but same timestamps and bytes transferred. Looks like both projects were billed for the same VPC-NAT hop during a shared migration job.
Maria S: Immediate mitigation: pin static regional IPs for the GPU pool, disable public IP assignment on instance create, and force internal-only draining to avoid external NAT egress.
Jess (FinOps): I'll open a support case with cloud provider for duplicate charge + request credits. Ticket template: "Unexpected EIP reassignment network egress billed twice across projects during autoscaling event (Feb 14)." Assigning to cloud-support-12345.
Alex K: Can someone add a short postmortem in incidents/ and update the autoscaler runbook to avoid ephemeral external IP churn?
Samir Patel: I'll add a guard in the terraform module to set nat_ip = null and use internal load balancer for termination. Also adding a monitoring alert for >200GB inter-zone transfer in 1h.
Jess (FinOps): Filing refund request now. If support denies, we'll escalate to our account rep. Also adding allocation of the unexpected cost to the infra incident bucket for this month.
Maria S: :facepalm: and :eyes: — lesson learned. Thanks for the quick triage.
Alex K: Thanks all. Please post updates in this thread when support replies and after the runbook and terraform changes land.
